This directly causes the 42.9% idle issue slots and the 33.68% occupancy gap. The grid is (1, 2048): a single CTA in X covers all 9 elements, so the entire X dimension is serialized into one block. Switching to XBLOCK=16 (next power-of-two >= 9) and increasing YBLOCK (e.g., 32 or 64) will: (a) eliminate wasted threads in X, (b) increase Y-parallelism per block for better occupancy, and (c) improve memory coalescing on the Y dimension. Adding @triton.autotune lets the runtime find the optimal combination.

applicable_when: The kernel is a weight-tensor transpose/reshape (32x512x3x3 filter, channel-last to channel-first). xnumel=9 (the 3x3 spatial dimension) is tiny, yet XBLOCK=128 is used — this means 119 of 128 threads per block are masked off on every load/store, wasting 93% of thread slots. Meanwhile YBLOCK=8 is far too small to saturate the Y dimension (16384 elements). The result is only ~1 wave across 132 SMs, 66% achieved occupancy, and poor sector utilization (18/32 bytes). Switching to XBLOCK=1 (or 2) and YBLOCK=32–128 eliminates wasted masked threads, increases the number of active CTAs, and improves coalescing on the Y-strided store pattern. @triton.autotune will find the optimal combination at runtime.
